composition.note: 013000 opening places formation in something like the eighth or seventh century BCE and stresses debated oral composition/transcription. This date is not the legendary Trojan War; the Odyssey is not automatically assigned the Iliad’s date.
composition.label: 8th–7th centuries BCE · debated formation

setting.label: c. 1200 BCE · conventional Trojan heroic frame
setting.note: Conventional Bronze Age frame for the Trojan War and its aftermath; this is a sorting anchor, not a claim that the war or marvelous voyages happened in this year. The poems mix periods. Their formation and surviving witnesses are separate. See discovery-homeric-setting and the 013000 opening; British Museum Troy exhibition notes that Homer’s war has not been established as a historical event.

creators.name: Homer
creators.note: Traditional attribution of a layered and transmitted text; not proof of a single historical author.

description: Recounts Books 18–24 of the Iliad, from Achilles’ grief and new shield through his return, Hector’s death, Patroclus’ funeral games and Priam’s ransom appeal. Explores the shield’s images of law and ordinary life, revenge, the treatment of the dead, women’s laments and the temporary truce that makes Hector’s burial possible.
